seo_title: Cost of Living in Istanbul 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Istanbul per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A bridge between Europe and Asia and one of the most popular cities for Russians relocating. Visa-free for 60 days, an active IT community and affordable food — though rent keeps rising.
pros: Visa-free for 60 days with the option to extend
Street food among the best in the world and very affordable
A large Russian-speaking and IT community
Direct flights anywhere — a hub airport
A historic atmosphere where two continents meet
cons: A seismic zone — Istanbul is at risk of earthquakes
Huge traffic jams at rush hour
The language barrier is stronger than it seems

faq.question: Does the MIR card work in Istanbul?
faq.answer: No, you need Visa/Mastercard or a local Ziraat / Vakıfbank card.

faq.question: Which district should I choose in Istanbul?
faq.answer: Kadıköy (the Asian side) — trendy and calmer. Şişli and Beşiktaş are on the European side, closer to the action.

faq.question: Is the lira falling fast in Istanbul?
faq.answer: Yes, inflation is high. It's better to earn your salary in foreign currency; rent is usually indexed annually.

faq.question: Is it dangerous with earthquakes in Istanbul?
faq.answer: There is a risk. Buildings since 2000 are constructed to code. Older ones are less reliable.

faq.question: Is English used day to day in Istanbul?
faq.answer: In Kadıköy, Karaköy and Beşiktaş — yes. In the old city and outside the centre you'll need some Turkish phrases.

faq.question: How much is long-term rent in Istanbul?
faq.answer: A one-bedroom in the centre is 70,000–110,000 ₽ — rising by 30–50% every year.

reviews.text: Istanbul is pure energy. Kadıköy on the Asian side is cheaper and calmer. Renting is stressful — it's indexed every year.
Eastern Europe and Asia at once. The downside — opening a bank account without an ikamet is nearly impossible.
